getLawyer.why: Thailand imposes HEAVY penalties for drugs — up to the DEATH PENALTY for trafficking. Police do spot checks, search belongings, and may require urine samples. Contact your embassy and a lawyer immediately; say and sign nothing without counsel and an interpreter.
E-cigarettes/vapes are ILLEGAL to import, possess or use in Thailand — up to 10 years in jail or heavy fines. Do not bring or use them. If caught, contact your embassy and a lawyer.

Lèse-majesté: insulting the king or royal family (including online) is a serious crime with lengthy prison sentences. Avoid any public or online comment on the monarchy. If accused, get a lawyer and your embassy immediately.

If arrested in Thailand, ask for your embassy, a lawyer, and an interpreter. Note Thailand does not recognize dual citizenship — if they consider you Thai, consular help may be refused. Say nothing without counsel.

deadlines.title: Visa-free stay — 30 days (extendable 30)
deadlines.rule: Canadian tourists get up to 30 DAYS visa-free on arrival, extendable once by up to 30 more days at an Immigration Office (officer's discretion). Complete the Digital Arrival Card before arriving. Overstaying brings fines, detention, and bans.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — Thailand

sentencing.name: Drug offences (Thailand)
sentencing.first_offender: Heavy fines and long jail even for possession; trafficking can carry life or the DEATH PENALTY. A local lawyer is essential immediately.

sentencing.name: E-cigarette / vaping (Thailand)
sentencing.first_offender: Possession or use can mean heavy fines or jail; do not bring or use vapes.
sentencing.maximum: Up to 10 years in jail or heavy fines.

statutes.title: Carry ID at all times
statutes.summary: You must carry identification at all times; carry a photocopy of your passport bio page and entry stamp, though police may require the originals. Failing to produce ID can lead to detention. Never use your passport as rental collateral.

statutes.title: Lèse-majesté — insulting the monarchy
statutes.summary: Offensive or insulting words/actions toward the king or royal family (including online) are illegal and carry lengthy prison sentences. Avoid any comment on the monarchy, politics, or the military.

book.title: Police, ID, and if you're detained in Thailand
book.overview: Thailand has strict laws and severe drug penalties. Carry ID at all times. Tourist Police (1155) speak English and help visitors. If detained, ask for your embassy, a lawyer, and an interpreter — and note Thailand does NOT recognize dual citizenship, which can limit consular help. Emergencies: 191 police, 1669 medical, 199 fire.
your_rights: Carry ID always; police may require the original passport.
If arrested, ask for a lawyer, an interpreter, and your embassy.
Do not sign anything without a lawyer and translation.
Tourist Police (1155) assist visitors in English.
You have a right not to be mistreated.
key_steps: Carry your passport (and a copy); never hand it over as collateral.
If stopped, be calm and polite; comply procedurally.
If detained: ask for the embassy, a lawyer, and an interpreter.
Avoid drugs, vapes, and any comment on the monarchy.
common_mistakes: Bringing or using a vape (illegal, up to 10 years).
Any drug involvement (up to death penalty).
Assuming dual citizenship gets you Canadian consular help.
book.when_lawyer: Immediately for any arrest, drug, vape, or lèse-majesté matter — get your embassy and a local lawyer; treat drugs as a life-and-death emergency.

book.title: Entry and your 30 days in Thailand
book.overview: Canadians get 30 days visa-free, extendable once by up to 30 days. Complete the Digital Arrival Card before arriving. Overstaying brings fines, detention, and re-entry bans.
your_rights: Visa-free tourism 30 days, extendable 30 more (officer's discretion).
You're entitled to your entry stamp.
You can apply to extend at an Immigration Office.
key_steps: Complete the Digital Arrival Card before arrival.
Track your 30 days; extend before they run out.
Keep your passport and entry stamp safe.
For work/study/longer stays, get a Thai visa in advance.
book.when_lawyer: For overstays, visa problems, or detention, consult a Thai lawyer via the embassy.

book.title: Serious offences in Thailand (drugs, vaping, lèse-majesté)
book.overview: Thailand punishes drugs up to the death penalty, bans vapes (up to 10 years), and criminalizes insulting the monarchy (lèse-majesté). These catch tourists off guard. Avoid them entirely; if accused, get a lawyer and your embassy at once.
your_rights: Right to a lawyer, an interpreter, and to contact your embassy.
Presumption of innocence, but pre-trial detention is common.
key_steps: Do not bring or use vapes/e-cigarettes.
Never touch illegal drugs — penalties are extreme.
Do not comment on the monarchy, online or in person.
If accused, say nothing and get a lawyer + embassy immediately.
book.when_lawyer: Immediately — a local criminal lawyer and your embassy; drug matters are life-and-death.

book.title: Emergencies and staying safe in Thailand
book.overview: Tourist Police 1155 (English); 191 police, 1669 medical, 199 fire. Main risks: motorbike accidents (Canada advises against riding), scams, and strict laws. Avoid riding motorcycles, watch drinks, and respect local laws.
your_rights: You can report crime to Thai police where it happened before leaving.
key_steps: Avoid renting/riding motorcycles (insurance often void without a licence).
In danger, call emergency services, then the embassy.
common_mistakes: Riding a motorbike without the right licence (injury + void insurance).
Underestimating how strict the laws are.
book.when_lawyer: For injury, a serious crime, or any detention, contact your embassy for local lawyer referrals.
